quest.title: The Moon Adorning the Night: The Three Moons
quest.description: Columbina seems to have something she wants to do in the Silvermoon Hall...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Columbina! You seem to be in a good mood today!

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hah... Come on up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You wanna play Moon Chess again or something?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yes. It has been a while, and I somewhat miss playing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are the rules the same as before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or, can you move multiple pieces per turn now because you're the Trilune Goddess?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: That would be cheating.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, yeah, Paimon knows that! She was just kidding.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Shall we begin, then?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And so, you and Columbina had a wonderful time playing the game together...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: The three moons, linked up in a line...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Still thinking about how that last match went?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Oh, no. It's just... Looking back on the game now gives me a peculiar feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah. Now that you have the power of three moons, you've become more than just something that can dominate the night sky.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yes. And I also think... that the fate of the world may have been different, had there not been division between the three Moon Goddesses.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What were they like?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: The first one I saw was Sonnet, goddess of the Iridescent Moon. She was livelier than I'd imagined, more like a playful younger sister.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Aria of the Eternal Moon, was the most mature of the three. She was a natural leader, and was most gentle to others. Ah, just like Lauma, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: As for Canon of the Frost Moon... she seemed both wise and far-sighted. And it was she who gave her moon to me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like all of them were kind deities.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yes. Despite their differences, they loved Teyvat, and they love this home.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: When I spoke to them of the things to come, they all seemed relieved, glad that this world still held so rich a future.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: That was also why they gave me the power to return "home."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Paimon would love to see them, and give them a real proper "thank you"...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I would very much like that as well. But I fear it's no longer possible...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Fortunately, this world continues onward, and the humans they protected have survived, and pass on their stories to this day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! As long as we live well and don't let the bad guys destroy the world — that's the best thanks we can give 'em!

choices.text: You certainly have a way with words, Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! You can bet Paimon's always trying to live her best life!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You too, Columbina! Eat well and sleep well every day, and come find us if you wanna play games!

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: I suspect that from now on, I shall think of those three gentle goddesses every time I play Moon Chess...

choices.text: In that case, every day's a thanks-giving for you...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Perhaps... Like this?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me think...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Moons... Moons...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: How about here?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Looks like I won this round.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: My three moons are connected.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mm, this should win it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mm... The moons wax and wane in an endless cycle...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It seems both sets of moons refuse to be eclipsed.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Are we... heading for a tie?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ah, you weigh your decisions carefully before making them, I see. Take your time — we have plenty of that, after all.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Did you forget how to place your moons in the night sky? Shall I help you?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You don't like this game? Hm... I find it quite amusing myself.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mm? Are you staring at me? Your gaze is not subtle.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You're staring... Is the truth of the moons written on my face?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The board's over there, by the way...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hm, your moons are aligned.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The night sky is yours.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ah... I must have... slipped up somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You have a wonderful time playing the game with Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I shall carry on their moonlight...
